spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single DynamoDB-backed entity with ordinary CRUD only.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint fetching a single note
Note model has title, body and timestamps

plan.summary: A FastAPI REST service for managing personal notes. Clients create, list, fetch, update and delete notes; each note holds a title, body and created/updated timestamps. Notes persist in a single DynamoDB table that the service calls directly via boto3. No asynchronous, scheduled or event-driven processing is implied, so no queues, topics or Lambda functions are planned.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new note from a JSON body containing title and body; server generates the note id and created_at/updated_at timestamps and writes the item to DynamoDB.
List notes, scanning the DynamoDB table with optional limit and pagination cursor; returns an array of notes.
Fetch a single note by id; returns 404 if the item does not exist.
Update the title and/or body of an existing note and refresh updated_at; returns 404 if the item does not exist.
Delete a note by id; returns 204 on success and 404 if the item does not exist.
Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; reports service status and DynamoDB table reachability.

data_models.name: Note
fields: body: str (required, may be empty string)

data_models.name: NoteCreateRequest
fields: body: str (optional, defaults to empty string)

aws_resources.name: notes
aws_resources.justification: The specification states notes are stored in DynamoDB. Single table with partition key note_id (S), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, backing all five CRUD endpoints.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the backend service GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Scan and DescribeTable on the notes table only — least-privilege access used by the running application.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/personal-notes-api
aws_resources.justification: Log group the application writes request and error logs to for operational visibility of the CRUD API.

assumptions: Notes are not scoped per authenticated user; 'personal notes' is interpreted as a single-tenant API with no auth layer, since the spec mentions no authentication or user accounts.
Note identifiers are server-generated UUID4 strings used as the DynamoDB partition key; clients do not supply ids.
Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are server-generated ISO-8601 UTC strings; created_at is immutable and updated_at is refreshed on every successful update.

Listing uses a DynamoDB Scan with a default page size of 50 and an opaque cursor, which is acceptable for a personal-scale dataset; no GSI is needed because there are no secondary query patterns in the spec.
PUT performs a partial update (only supplied fields change) rather than a full replacement, which is the conventional behaviour for this kind of notes API.
The API is hosted by the evaluation harness as a standalone FastAPI service, so no Lambda or API Gateway resources are planned; the spec requires no asynchronous or event-driven processing.

No secrets are required because the service uses IAM/environment-provided credentials and the DynamoDB table name is supplied via environment variable (e.g. NOTES_TABLE_NAME), so Secrets Manager is not planned.
The DynamoDB endpoint is configurable via an AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable so the same code works against LocalStack and real AWS.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → personal_notes_api (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:notes, IAM:notes-api-app-role, CloudWatch:/cloudforge/personal-notes-api

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI notes service split into a route layer (`app.py`) and a storage abstraction (`storage.py`). `NotesRepository` defines the interface; `DynamoDBNotesRepository` uses boto3 (region default us-east-1, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` honoured, table from `NOTES_TABLE_NAME` defaulting to `notes`) with conditional writes mapping missing items to 404, opaque base64 scan cursors, and a `describe_table` health probe; `InMemoryNotesRepository` provides an equivalent offline implementation. Endpoints: POST/GET/PUT/DELETE `/notes` plus `/health`, with a uniform `{detail, code}` error body. Tests use `TestClient` with dependency overrides and a FakeTable stub, so no network or LocalStack is needed; boto3 client construction is verified via monkeypatch. Only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3 and pydantic are required.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the personal_notes_api plan, covering exactly the three planned AWS resources plus the CMK that satisfies encryption-at-rest checks.

- versions.tf: terraform block with required_version and hashicorp/aws pinned to ~> 5.0.
- variables.tf: defaults matching the plan names (table `notes`, role `notes-api-app-role`, log group `/cloudforge/personal-notes-api`), plus region, tags, billing mode, retention (365 days) and validation blocks.
- main.tf: provider with default_tags (project, managed-by); aws_dynamodb_table `notes` with `note_id` (S) partition key, PAY_PER_REQUEST, point-in-time recovery and SSE with a customer managed KMS key; aws_cloudwatch_log_group with KMS encryption and 365-day retention; aws_kms_key (rotation enabled, explicit key policy allowing account administration, DynamoDB service use and CloudWatch Logs use) with an alias; aws_iam_role + aws_iam_policy + attachment granting only GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Scan/DescribeTable on the notes table ARN, log-stream writes on that specific log group, and key usage on that one CMK — no wildcard actions or resources.
- outputs.tf: table name/ARN/hash key, role and policy ARNs, log group name/ARN, KMS key ARN and region, so the app can be wired via NOTES_TABLE_NAME.

No RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache, no Lambda or API Gateway (the plan hosts FastAPI standalone), and every resource traces to a planned aws_resources entry; the KMS key exists solely to encrypt the planned DynamoDB table and log group.
